version.changelog: Modernize read-only OAuth, pagination, retries, validation, freshness metadata, bounded queries, exports, and credential safety.

llm.summary: This skill is a read-only Google Search Console helper with disclosed OAuth setup and bounded API querying; the main residual risk is normal credential handling plus unpinned Python dependencies.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is limited to user-specified OAuth client and token paths, and network access is coherent with Google OAuth/Search Console API use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a small requirements.txt with Google API/OAuth libraries, but versions are lower-bound constraints rather than pinned hashes or a lockfile.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are explicit about using packaged helpers, treating returned data as untrusted, limiting OAuth to webmasters.readonly, bounding dates, pagination, retries, and avoiding indexing or sitemap mutations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The auth helper stores a reusable OAuth token under ~/.config/gsc/token.json, but this is disclosed, protected with 0600 file permissions, and not paired with background jobs, startup hooks, or hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Search Console analysis, and the artifacts implement only read-only Search Console operations: listing properties, Search Analytics rows, URL inspection state, and sitemaps.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable granting read-only access to your Google Search Console data. Keep the OAuth client secret and token files private, use an isolated Python environment, and consider pinning dependencies or using a lockfile before production use.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential-file handling is expected for an installed-app OAuth flow; the code validates ownership and permissions, rejects symlinks, uses the read-only Search Console scope, and warns users not to paste secrets into chat or command arguments.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not declare a separate permission manifest, but the artifact instructions and scripts are tightly scoped to packaged helpers, local credential paths, and Google Search Console read operations.
[RA2] expected: The cited persistence is an OAuth token file, not a scheduler, service, hook, or background process; it is disclosed and necessary for reuse of the Search Console integration.
[EA4] expected: The artifact specifically instructs not to retry indefinitely, and the query helper enforces retry, date, page, and result limits.
[SC1] unexpected: The unpinned Google dependencies are a real reproducibility and supply-chain weakness, but there is no artifact evidence of typosquatting, dependency confusion, remote payload execution, or malicious bundled code.
[T08] unexpected: The SARIF supply-chain warning is supported by requirements.txt using open-ended lower bounds; this warrants user caution but does not make the skill suspicious by itself.
